web.title: Australian resident for tax purposes
web.description:
# Australian resident for tax purposes
## Part-year Australian resident
If you are an Australian resident for part of the year, your [tax-free threshold](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/coming-to-australia-or-going-overseas/coming-to-australia/tax-free-threshold-for-newcomers-to-australia) will be less than the full tax-free threshold of $18,200 that applies to Australian residents.

If you became or ceased to be an Australian resident for tax purposes during the income year, you will receive the [part-year tax-free threshold](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/coming-to-australia-or-going-overseas/living-overseas-and-becoming-a-foreign-tax-resident) and resident tax rates will apply to your income.

Part-year residents have a tax-free threshold of at least $13,464. The remaining $4,736 of the full tax-free threshold is pro-rated according to the number of months during the income year you were a resident for tax purposes.

We will work out your tax-free threshold using the information you provide.

web.title: Living overseas and becoming a foreign tax-resident
web.description:
# Living overseas and becoming a foreign tax-resident
If you're leaving Australia and become a non-resident of Australia for tax purposes, your tax-free threshold for the year will be lower than the threshold available to most taxpayers who are Australian residents for the full year.

You're entitled to a tax-free threshold amount of $13,464 plus ($4,736 divided by 12, multiplied by the number of months you were an Australian resident for tax purposes, counting the month you left).

You can only claim the tax-free threshold while you are an Australian resident.

## Example: part-year resident tax-free threshold
She is entitled to 6 months (from July to December) of the tax-free threshold in the income year. Her tax-free threshold is:

- $13,464 + [($4,736 ÷ 12) × 6]

Britney would pay no tax on her first $15,832 of taxable income. She enters the 16% tax bracket after that and will have the [Australian resident tax rates](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-australian-residents) applied to her income for the year.

End of example

web.description:
# Tax-free threshold for newcomers to Australia
## Adjusted tax-free threshold
### Example: tax-free threshold for part-year resident
= $13,464 + (($4,736 × 3) ÷ 12)

= $13,464 + $1,184

= $14,648.

For any taxable income over $14,648, he will start to pay tax at the rate of 16%.

web.description:
# Your tax residency
## If your residency status changes during the year
You're entitled to a [pro-rata tax-free threshold](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/coming-to-australia-or-going-overseas/living-overseas-and-becoming-a-foreign-tax-resident) for the number of months you're an Australian resident.

web.description:
# Taxation of Australian resident WHMs from NDA countries
## Court decision
### What this decision means for you
#### Calculating how much tax to pay
##### Both Australian and foreign-sourced income
###### Example: resident WHM from an eligible NDA country who has both Australian and foreign-sourced income
- (Taxable income **minus** tax-free threshold) **multiplied by** tax rate **equals** tax on taxable income, which is (($28,000 + $1,500 + $500) − $18,200) × 16% = $1,888

## How to lodge or amend a tax return
### 2021–22 and future year tax return lodgments
- if applicable, the number of months you were an Australian resident (in the Adjustments section at the **question** about the part-year tax-free threshold)
